why: Passage B (6:4) restates the mishna's rule that liability requires both handing over to Molekh and passing through fire, with the exemptions for doing only one, while A only describes the basic prohibition and ritual.
SA EH 38:9 explicitly addresses the condition 'על מנת שירצה' (how it is interpreted) and the father's death leaving her betrothed, while 38:11 only deals with the son dying.
Passage B (3:11) codifies the witnesses' statement 'we never signed but one get with these names', matching Rabbi Yirmeya, while A deals with a known same-named man in town.

The note marks 'התולה תפיליו יתלו לו חייו', and SA OC 40:1 forbids hanging tefillin by the boxes or straps, while 40:3 deals with placing them under the head, which belongs to the other note on this line.

Passage B (2:7) says one may cover himself in murky water (מים עכורין) but not in clear water, which matches the Gemara's ruling at 'במים עכורין שנו'; Passage A is about dry excrement and urine absorbed in the ground.

Passage B (586:8) rules on a cracked shofar that was glued, including whether it is valid when glued, which is the mishna's ruling; Passage A (586:5) is about a vow forbidding benefit from a shofar and has nothing to do with it.

The marked Gemara says that when a husband tells a court to give a get, they write it and give it themselves, and Rambam 2:10 states this law (told to write and give, they write a valid get), whereas 2:6 covers telling them to instruct a scribe, which makes the get invalid.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Daily Offerings and Additional Offerings 6:7
add: Mishneh Torah, Daily Offerings and Additional Offerings 7:7
why: The note marks 'לקצירת העומר' (reaping the omer all night), which Passage B (7:7) states almost verbatim, while Passage A (6:7) covers libation and trumpet blasts and has nothing to do with the omer.
Rambam 24:9 rules that one of two same-named Yosef ben Shimon in a town may collect on a note from others, matching 'מוציאין שטר חוב על אחרים', while 24:8 deals with the restrictions between the two.

The Gemara ruling that a mistaken tear counts as rending if the truth is learned within toch kedei dibbur, and not after it, is codified in Mourning 8:8; 1:8 deals with a nefel (a stillborn or premature infant) and has no connection to it.

Rambam 6:16 states the ruling at the marked words (acquire the field on condition that you write the deed, so he can retract from both until the deed arrives), while 6:14 concerns a bond transferred along with land.

The note is marked at 'אינו נאמן ולא אמרן', where the Gemara limits the rule to a homeowner not apt to sell and to items not typically concealed. Passage B (SA 90:11) codifies exactly that, while Passage A (90:12) covers the later ruling on items typically lent or rented, which belongs to another note.

The marked words say the wall boards were permitted only to festival pilgrims, which is exactly Rambam 17:30 ('לא התירו הפסים... אלא לבהמת עולי רגלים בלבד'), whereas 17:32 deals with filling a bucket and the manger decree of Abaye.
Rambam 4:11 repeats the Gemara's words almost verbatim: the fetus is buried to publicize that the animal is exempt from the firstborn, while 4:12 deals with the 30-day conception interval.
Passage B states that anyone who reduces below 200/100 has a 'bi'at zenut', matching the marked words, whereas Passage A gives only the minimum amounts and omits the consequence.
Only Mishneh Torah Marriage 10:9 states that whoever reduces below 200/100 has engaged in 'bi'at zenut', matching the marked words, while 10:7 gives just the minimum amounts.

The marked words say all women, even those who cannot be pregnant (barren, minor, husband overseas or imprisoned), must wait three months, and 11:20 lists exactly these cases while 11:18 gives only the general rule.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Rest on a Holiday 3:6
add: Mishneh Torah, Rest on a Holiday 3:7
why: Passage B (Rambam 3:7) restates the Gemara's ruling almost word for word: scalding and singing the head and feet, no clay, earth or lime, no shearing with scissors, while Passage A (3:6) covers skinning and the 'marigil' ruling instead.

remove: Mishneh Torah, The Sanhedrin and the Penalties within Their Jurisdiction 11:6
add: Mishneh Torah, The Sanhedrin and the Penalties within Their Jurisdiction 18:6
why: Passage B (Sanhedrin 18:6) restates the marked ruling (stealing a temple vessel, cursing by a sorcerer, intercourse with an Aramean woman, with zealots striking), while Passage A is about the order of judges' voting.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Prayer and the Priestly Blessing 13:17
add: Mishneh Torah, Prayer and the Priestly Blessing 12:17
why: The Gemara words ask whether the maftir counts toward the seven readers, and Rambam 12:17 rules 'מפטיר עולה מהמנין שהרי הוא קורא בתורה'; 13:17 only covers Chanukah and Purim readings.
Shulchan Arukh OC 301:7 says one may not go out with a single shoe unless he has a wound on his foot, which is the marked ruling, while 301:6 is about crossing water to guard fruit.
The marked words concern non-ordained courts compelling divorces as agents, which matches B (lawful compulsion by any court in every place and time), whereas A deals with compulsion by gentiles.

The marked words say the buyer takes three swarms one after another, then one and leaves one; Passage B (23:13) restates this nearly verbatim, while Passage A concerns how much to leave from the offspring of mothers and daughters, which is a different ruling.

Passage B (24:8) ends with 'היו שניהם לוים שניהם כהנים יכתבו דורות', which restates the marked ruling; Passage A is about writing documents without the other party present and says nothing about priests or generations.
The note is at 'אסורים בהספד', and SA 696:3 states that the 14th and 15th are forbidden for eulogy and fasting, while 696:1 deals only with the separate ruling on work.

Passage B (21:8) restates the Gemara's ruling almost word for word, that a niddah does all her husband's tasks except pouring the cup, making the bed and washing his face, hands and feet. Passage A (21:5) covers other tasks a wife does when poor and says nothing about a niddah.
The Gemara words 'הרי זה גיטך על מנת שתאכלי בשר חזיר' match Rambam 6:8, which rules that a condition to eat pig meat in a get is valid and binding, while 7:8 deals with defects and vows in kiddushin.

Passage B (5:14) restates both Rava rulings, permitting a fee to have someone lend (the Torah forbids only interest from borrower to lender) and 'shachar amirah', while Passage A (5:16) is about renting out dinars and is unrelated.

Passage B restates Rava's reasoning that a person is careful with his document only up to three years, which is what the marked words say, while A deals with the three-year chazaka and the failure to protest.
Passage B (1:25) opens 'גט שיש עליו עדים ואין בו זמן' and rules it invalid, matching the marked words, while A deals with which date and place the witnesses write when delayed.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Ownerless Property and Gifts 10:7
add: Mishneh Torah, Ownerless Property and Gifts 10:5
why: The note's letter marks 'הרי שראו את אביהן שהטמין מעות...', the father's statement as one who relays versus one who employs artifice, which Passage B (10:5) restates almost word for word, while Passage A (10:7) codifies the later dream case that begins 'הרי שהיה מצטער'.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Things Forbidden on the Altar 7:10
add: Mishneh Torah, Things Forbidden on the Altar 7:6
why: Passage B (7:6) rules out wine from the barrel's mouth and bottom for libations, matching the marked words, while Passage A concerns menorah oil pressings.

The marked words distinguish thick from thin mixtures (thick is food and takes mezonot, thin is medicine and takes shehakol), which is exactly Shulchan Arukh OC 208:6; 208:8 concerns millet and legume bread.

Passage B (Sabbath 25:12) restates the mishna's ruling that shards of vessels may be moved if they serve a similar function, with the barrel and cruse-cover examples, while Passage A concerns vessel covers.

The note marks 'ניסת לכהן אוכלת בתרומה', and Passage B (6:3) rules that an Israelite girl, even aged three, who marries a priest eats terumah, while Passage A (7:3) is about a pure priest eating impure terumah.

Passage B (392:4) rules that a partition (mazeva) at the alley's entrance means that alley does not prohibit the others, which is Rav Chisda's dika ruling, whereas A deals with ladders and the garbage heap, which belong to a different line.

The Gemara's baraita (told his father died, he tore, then it turned out his son died) is codified in Mishneh Torah, Mourning 8:8, which says almost the same thing, while 1:8 is about stillborn and eight-month infants.

The Mishna's marked words (widow with a 200 ketubah selling property worth 100 for 200, or worth 200 for 100, has received her ketubah) match Rambam 17:15 almost word for word; 17:14 covers a different ruling, a widow selling privately at a fair price.

The marked Gemara words (הוציאוה, עזבוה, התירוה, הניחוה, הועילו) are the doubtful expressions, and Rambam 2:11 rules these cases are a doubtful divorce, while 2:10 covers the unmarked wording like פטרוה and עשו לה כדת.

The marked words (מקום שנהגו להדליק... אין מדליקין) are restated nearly verbatim in 610:1, while 610:3 only covers the separate ruling on synagogues, dark alleys and the sick, which belongs to a different note.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Ownerless Property and Gifts 8:10
add: Mishneh Torah, Ownerless Property and Gifts 8:12
why: The marked words qualify the 'write and give' case (no deed after death), which is stated in B (8:12), while A concerns a deathbed gift with a kinyan, matching the earlier 'kanu minei' clause.
Rambam 3:13 rules that a minor betrothed without her father's consent is not betrothed even if he later agrees, which matches Ravina's case; 3:15 is about agents and witnesses.

Rambam 2:10 rules that if he says to two or more 'write a get and give it to my wife,' they themselves write and give it, which matches the marked words; 2:6 is about telling a scribe and witnesses, so it does not.

Passage B (21:28) states the ruling at the marked words, that one may smear and rub the intestines on Shabbat if done together and not as on a weekday, while Passage A (21:21) is about eating and drinking things that healthy people do not.

Rav Chisda's 'thought is not speech' ruling is codified in 62:3, which requires pronouncing Shema with the lips ('ובלבד שיוציא בשפתיו'), whereas 62:4 only allows reciting in the heart in cases of duress.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Shofar, Sukkah and Lulav 6:6
add: Mishneh Torah, Shofar, Sukkah and Lulav 6:10
why: Note ד marks the ruling that one who went down because of rain need not return until he finishes his meal, which is stated in Rambam 6:10 (B) and not in 6:6 (A), which only gives the general rule of eating and sleeping in the sukkah.
The marked words say the wall-boards were permitted only for festival pilgrims (and their animals), which Rambam 17:30 states almost verbatim; 17:32 covers the manger decree from 20b:6-7.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Prayer and the Priestly Blessing 8:8
add: Mishneh Torah, Prayer and the Priestly Blessing 8:7
why: Rambam 8:7 says all must be in one place to join for prayer and a separating partition prevents joining, matching the Gemara, while 8:8 deals with excrement in a room.
Shulchan Arukh EH 38:12 restates the mishna's law of betrothal on condition of acting as a laborer or speaking to the authorities, while 38:10 deals with conditions about the father's consent.

The Gemara's ruling that a disqualified sin offering's blood needs no laundering, whether or not it had a period of fitness (left overnight, impure, or taken out), is restated almost word for word in Mishneh Torah 8:3 (B); 8:2 (A) only covers which garments and offerings need laundering.
Rambam 22:20 rules one dries with a towel and carries it in hand without concern for wringing, matching R. Shimon at the marked words, whereas 22:19 deals with wiping muddy hands.

Passage B (1:3) opens with 'כל הקודם בנחלה יוצאי ירכו קודמין' and states that the father precedes his descendants and the father's father precedes the father's brother, whereas A (1:2) only says a father inherits a childless son and a mother does not inherit her sons.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Offerings for Unintentional Transgressions 11:6
add: Mishneh Torah, Offerings for Unintentional Transgressions 11:7
why: Rambam 11:7 ends with the Gemara's own wording 'בטמאת מקדש וקדשיו עשו ספק ידיעה כידיעה', matching the marked words, while 11:6 deals with the forgotten-path case.
CM 375:5 explicitly says a husband in his minor wife's nichsei melog is like a yored birshut, matching the marked ruling, while 375:8 deals with the oath on expenses from later Gemara lines.
576:9 rules that they sound the alarm over the guvai (a kind of locust) for any amount but not over the chagav, which matches the marked words, while 576:8 deals with blight and mildew.

B restates the mishna's ruling on the dangerously ill, the one taken out in a neck chain, the sailor and the caravan traveler who say 'write a get', while A deals with a healthy man who kills himself.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Leavened and Unleavened Bread 2:9
add: Mishneh Torah, Leavened and Unleavened Bread 4:9
why: Rambam 4:9 restates the tanners' bowl ruling (flour placed within three days must be removed, earlier or with hides is permitted), while 2:9 is about a child carrying bread and crumbs.

Mishnah's perforated gullet, brain membrane and heart-to-chamber rulings are codified in 6:1's list of eleven organs whose perforation into the cavity makes a tereifa, whereas 7:1 deals with lung membranes.

Passage B (18:6) states that chametz, emancipation and consecration abrogate a lien and adds the betterment-of-the-world rule for the slave, matching the marked words, whereas A covers only consecration.
Passage B cites 'lo tisna' and rules that only hatred in the heart is prohibited, not hitting or insulting, which matches the Gemara's derivation from 'bilvavkha'; A concerns rebuke.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Vessels of the Sanctuary and Those Who Serve Therein 1:1
add: Mishneh Torah, Vessels of the Sanctuary and Those Who Serve Therein 8:1
why: Rambam 8:1 lists the four garments of the ordinary priest (tunic, trousers, cap, belt), matching the Gemara's 'high priest serves in eight garments, ordinary in four', while 1:1 is about anointing oil.

Passage B (11:21) states that a convert and his wife must wait ninety days 'to distinguish between seed sown in sanctity and seed not sown in sanctity', which matches the Gemara words, while Passage A (11:19) only covers counting the waiting period from the date the get was written.
Passage B (12:5) states 'ואם בא הקנאי לטל רשות מבית דין להרגו אין מורין לו', which restates the Gemara's 'הבא לימלך אין מורין לו', while Passage A (12:8) says nothing about consulting the court.

Rambam 6:7 rules that a convert who converted on the 14th is like one who separates from the grave and gets no Paschal offering slaughtered for him, which matches 'הפורש מן הערלה כפורש מן הקבר', while 10:7 is about breaking the bone of the fat tail and is unrelated.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Prayer and the Priestly Blessing 13:17
add: Mishneh Torah, Prayer and the Priestly Blessing 12:17
why: The Gemara says the maftir reads from the Torah first and whether he counts toward the seven readers; Rambam 12:17 says 'the maftir counts toward the quorum since he reads in the Torah', while 13:17 only covers Chanukah and Purim readings.
The note's Rambam 9:1 concerns the vow about cooked food (permitted roasted/boiled), which matches SA 217:1; 217:2 on ma'aseh kedera matches Rambam 9:7, a different note.

The marked words state that a rabbinic-level obligation can discharge another rabbinic-level obligation, which is the content of 5:16 (ate without being satisfied, so a minor, slave, or woman may discharge it), while 5:15 only says a son may bless for his father.
The Mishnah concerns offerings made in a vessel (pan/deep pan) with three oil placements, which is what Rambam 13:6 describes, whereas 13:5 covers the plain solet offering.

remove: Mishneh Torah, First Fruits and other Gifts to Priests Outside the Sanctuary 11:16
add: Mishneh Torah, First Fruits and other Gifts to Priests Outside the Sanctuary 11:14
why: Halakha 11:14 states that one who miscarries fish, locusts, or a fortieth-day miscarriage is followed by a firstborn for the priest who must be redeemed, which matches the Mishnah. Halakha 11:16 deals with a Caesarean birth (yotzei dofen) and does not cover this ruling.

Passage B (Sales 21:5) restates the mishna's ruling on selling or contracting for a plot for a bridal house or widowhood home, built four cubits by six, while Passage A is about selling wheat at market price.

The Gemara words rule that the wife of an Israelite performs ḥalitza while the wife of a priest does not; SA 164:8 states this directly (if she married a priest, no ḥalitza is performed for her), whereas 164:7 deals with a child born after six months and the doubtful mamzer.

234:20 rules that after divorce, even if he remarried her on the day of hearing, he cannot annul, matching the Gemara's 'divorce is like ratification', while 234:21 only covers the day-of-hearing timing.

remove: Mishneh Torah, The Sanhedrin and the Penalties within Their Jurisdiction 22:7
add: Mishneh Torah, The Sanhedrin and the Penalties within Their Jurisdiction 22:9
why: Passage B (22:9) restates the Gemara's procedure: the judges finish the matter, the litigants are brought in, and the greatest judge says 'you are innocent/you are liable', while A concerns a judge revealing his vote afterward.

Rambam 6:16 codifies the rectum (חלחלת) perforation rule, kosher if the hole is at the place attached to the hips, which is Zeiri's ruling and R. Yohanan's measure; 6:15 covers intestines that came out or were overturned, which is unrelated.

Passage B (YD 218:4) restates the Mishnah's case of someone pressing a friend to eat and the friend vowing against entering the house or tasting cold water, ruling it permitted; Passage A (211:4) is about annulment of vows and has nothing to do with this case.

Passage B (4:16) covers eating the condition loaf first and then the forbidden loaf intentionally with liability, matching the marked words, whereas A (4:18) covers the interdependent loaves (תלאן זו בזו) of the later lines.

The Gemara words say liability for me'ilah applies only to Temple-maintenance property and burnt offerings, derived from 'nefesh ki timol ma'al... mikodshei Hashem'. Halakha 1:3 codifies this, citing that verse and covering sacred items of both the altar and Temple maintenance, while 1:2 only discusses items that were permitted for eating.

The Gemara ruling is that one witness says the husband died, she is permitted to remarry, and a second single witness says he did not die, so she does not leave her permitted state; Rambam 12:18 states exactly this, while 12:20 deals with different cases (two witnesses, women, or disqualified witnesses contradicting).

Rambam 24:8 states the ruling at the marked words (a receipt found among one's documents for 'the note of Yosef ben Shimon' makes both notes paid), while 24:1 only covers writing documents in the absent party's presence.

Passage B restates the ruling at the marked words, where a Jew buys a field from a gentile before it reaches a third, sells it back after, and the produce is still obligated because it became obligated in Jewish hands; Passage A is about a sharecropper sending produce and does not address this.
The marked words are Rav Yosef's 'where the forbidden item is, we penalize', which matches Rambam 8:6 (buyer penalized, slave freed), while 8:10 codifies the fled-slave story that follows.
The note marks the general principle 'אין איסור חל על איסור', which Rambam 17:8 states explicitly together with the 'מוסיף' exception, while 17:9 only applies it to the widow-to-zona case.
Passage B (YD 246:4) codifies dividing one's study into thirds for Scripture, Mishna and Talmud, matching the marked words, while Passage A (247:4) is about tzedakah.

The Gemara says that holding the scroll and saying only 'bah' counts as saying 'what is written in it'. Passage B (Vows 1:28) states exactly this ('נטלה בידו ונדר בה'), while Passage A covers a vow by the Torah without holding it, which is not the marked ruling.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Appraisals and Devoted Property 6:2
add: Mishneh Torah, Appraisals and Devoted Property 6:1
why: The marked words say that unspecified dedications (סתם חרמים) go to the priest, and Rambam 6:1 states exactly this ('חרם סתם הרי אלו לכהנים'), whereas 6:2 deals with how much of one's property may be dedicated.
Only 150:2 states that the money paid under a void sale bill is merely like an oral loan (מלוה על פה), which is the ruling at the marked words; 150:1 only covers pledge-holder's lack of chazaka.
Rambam 5:6 restates Abaye's ruling on two nested courtyards with higher outer walls, while 5:7 covers only the baskets case, which is the Gemara's later contrast.

The marked words are the mishna's 'hand needle to extract a thorn'; Rambam 25:8 states that a whole hand needle may be moved to remove a thorn, whereas 25:10 deals with vessels set aside because of a prohibition.
The note marks the ruling on hair for kneading clay (and lime for the smallest girl's finger), which Rambam Sabbath 18:11 states almost word for word, while 18:9 is about ink and quills.

The marked words set a virgin's ketubah at 200 and a widow's at a maneh, with the husband's claim of non-virginity believed, which matches 68:1 (tenet betulim only where the ketubah is 200), while 68:8 covers the tosafot and oath.

Passage B (164:7) restates the ruling at the marked words: a child born after the levirate marriage is a doubtful nine-month child of the first husband or seven-month child of the second, so she leaves with a get and the child is valid. Passage A (164:6) deals with a child whose months are unknown or who is a nefel.
Halakha 3:11 states almost verbatim 'נקב יש בו בצד אות פלונית' as a סימן מבהק, while 3:9 covers only place of loss and recognition by size, with no such sign.
Rambam 5:5 states the rulings on chamber blood (impure), upper-story blood (pure) and corridor blood (impure by presumption from the source), while 5:3 only defines the anatomy.

The marked words infer that the husband is believed if the father brings no proof for blemishes that may have arisen after betrothal while she is in her father's house, which is stated in 117:8, not the certainly-pre-betrothal blemishes of 117:7.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Offerings for Those with Incomplete Atonement 4:2
add: Mishneh Torah, Offerings for Those with Incomplete Atonement 5:2
why: The marked words say a guilt-offering slaughtered not for its own sake, or whose blood was not put on the thumbs, is offered on the altar with libations and the leper needs another guilt-offering. Passage B (5:2) restates exactly this, while Passage A (4:2) only describes the normal procedure.

The marked words 'even if he is presumed to have a brother' match SA EH 156:6, which says one who says 'this is my son' is believed to exempt his wife even if known to have brothers; 157:6 covers the 'not presumed to have brothers' case.

Passage B (409:6) codifies the doubtful-eiruv rule: if the teruma became impure before dark it is invalid, if after dark it is valid, and a doubtful eiruv is valid when it has a presumption of fitness. Passage A (409:10) covers a different subject, an agent placing the eiruv in the wrong place or with the wrong food.
Passage B (8:15) states that group members may not resume eating after falling asleep, which matches 'נרדמו לא יאכלו', while Passage A covers anointing with oil and roasting two lambs together.
The Gemara concerns a craftsman holding a cloak who can claim it was bought or never given, which is what SA 89:5 states; 89:4 only covers a wage-amount dispute.
The marked words say Hatov Vehametiv requires others drinking with him, which is what SA OC 175:4 states, while 178:4 concerns changing place and Birkat Hamazon.
Rambam 3:12 states the ruling at the marked words (גרף של רעי ועביט של מי רגלים forbidden for Shema even when empty), while 2:12 concerns reciting Shema out of order or while drowsy.
The Gemara case is a definite claim answered by 'I don't know' (exempt, with an oath where there is a connection), which is Rambam 1:8; 1:7 concerns a plaintiff who is himself uncertain.
The Gemara words 'אין מקבלין צאן ברזל מישראל מפני שהוא רבית' are codified in Rambam 8:12, while 8:13 deals with a hired cow priced in case it dies.
The marked words state the rule of three groups of thirty derived from kahal, edah, Yisrael, which Rambam 1:9 codifies; 1:11 covers the fifty minimum and the entering and closing of the courtyard.

The marked words begin 'משלה', and SA 80:11 says that if they did not add foods good for milk she must eat from her own; 80:12 concerns craving more than the fixed allowance, which belongs to the preceding words.

The marked words say children may read by candlelight because fear of their teacher keeps them from adjusting the wick, which is Shulchan Arukh 275:6; 275:7 is about reading Bameh Madlikin and does not fit.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 1:6
add: Mishneh Torah, Admission into the Sanctuary 1:7
why: The marked words (Abaye: priests drink wine nowadays like Rabbi, 'his repair is his ruin') match Rambam 1:7, which says a priest who knows neither his mishmar nor his beit av is by law forbidden wine forever, but 'tikkunato kilkulato' lets him drink always; 1:6 only covers the mishmar men's nights and days.
SA OC 448:3 opens with the exact ruling at the marked words (a Jew's chametz after Pesach is forbidden for benefit), while 445:3 deals with disposing of chametz before the prohibited time.
The Gemara concerns a niddah making the bed not in front of him and pouring the cup with a change, which is exactly Rambam Ishut 21:8; 21:5 only lists a wife's labors for a poor husband.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Daily Offerings and Additional Offerings 10:7
add: Mishneh Torah, Daily Offerings and Additional Offerings 10:8
why: The marked words ('ולמנסך אומר לו הגבה ידך... נסך על רגליו ורגמוהו באתרוגיהן') are restated almost word for word in 10:8, while 10:7 covers pouring water into wine, the basins and the perforations, which belong to the other note on the line.
Rambam 4:16 states that a mound 10 tefachim high, 4 or more from the balcony, is shared by both and prohibits both; 4:15 lacks this ruling.

Passage B (20:2) rules that one who seizes movable property for a creditor acquires it for him, unless the debtor owes other creditors, which is the ruling at 'התופס לבעל חוב'; Passage A deals with oaths and debtors hiding assets.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Daily Offerings and Additional Offerings 9:7
add: Mishneh Torah, Daily Offerings and Additional Offerings 9:9
why: The Gemara words 'פרים קודמין לאילים, ואילים לכבשים, כבשים לשעירים' match Passage B, which states this order of precedence and gives its reasons; Passage A deals with the order of the festival offerings and the sin-offerings for idolatry.

Passage B (7:6) rules that a bird burnt offering with one siman pinched below and one above is invalid, which matches the Gemara; Passage A is about a bird sin offering brought for a doubt and does not address this case.

remove: Mishneh Torah, Appraisals and Devoted Property 6:29
add: Mishneh Torah, Appraisals and Devoted Property 6:28
